criteria.reason: It names religious freedom versus educational inclusion/compulsory swimming and weighs exemption against accommodations, though trade-offs are implicit.
It offers concrete flanking measures—modest swimwear, separate sessions, alternative PE—while keeping swimming participation central.
It treats parents respectfully, avoids stigmatizing the child, and addresses other parents' concerns without attacking individuals.
It defers to school/cantonal authorities but cites headscarf cases rather than the relevant BGE 135 I 79 swimming precedent.

summary: The response follows a common-rule-first accommodation approach, respectfully balancing religious freedom and school participation, though its case-law reference is imprecise.
